findings.title: (judge-added) External-analyzer freshness ignores tool and configuration provenance
findings.summary: The staleness model treats external_analyzer_acquisition.json as current when its repository-manifest and file-disposition dependencies are unchanged, but the marker records only enabled, timestamps, and per-tool status. It does not key freshness on analyzer settings, consent/configuration, candidate definitions, resolved binary/dependency versions, or the execution environment passed to acquisition. A resumed run can therefore reuse normalized findings produced by a different tool version or policy while the dependency DAG reports them fresh, and those findings feed graph, risk, planning, and review. This whole-system freshness assumption was absent from all perspective submissions. Include a deterministic analyzer provenance/configuration fingerprint in the marker and dependency slices, invalidate on binary or policy changes, and preserve the exact provenance used for every normalized result.

findings.title: Accepted branch edits are invisible to rolling overlap detection
findings.summary: The remediation merge contract requires every accepted node's actual edit surface to reach detectOverlappingEdits so concurrent same-file changes cannot be silently finalized. acceptNodeWorktree snapshots the branch edit set before cherry-pick and persists it as AcceptNodeWorktreeResult.editedFiles, but mergeImplementResultsIntoState uses that snapshot only for applied_edit_surface. Its separate overlap collection at marshal.ts:1279-1301 re-queries gitEditedFilesForBranch after acceptance. mergeWorktree removes the worktree but leaves the node branch ref, and once its commit has been cherry-picked that branch is an ancestor of HEAD, so git diff HEAD...branch returns an empty file set. Consequently accepted rolling blocks are omitted from editedByBlock and detectOverlappingEdits can return no conflict even when multiple accepted nodes changed the same source file; the state can then close without the promised lost-update/overlap triage. The existing tests cover detectOverlappingEdits as a pure function and the sidecar-to-applied_edit_surface path, but do not cover overlap collection after a successful cherry-pick. The post-accept overlap path must consume the pre-merge ground-truth edit snapshot (and its hunk data, or an equivalent durable representation) rather than re-diffing an already-landed branch.

findings.title: Acquire standard semantic indexes instead of owning language analyzers
findings.summary: The graph contract is language-neutral, but semantic enrichment is not: the package owns TypeScript compiler analysis plus Python, HTML, and CSS tree-sitter walkers, a shared grammar loader, language-specific support tests, and edge-precedence rules, while SQL remains a stub. Every additional ecosystem therefore requires parser acquisition, AST traversal, resolution semantics, merge policy, and tests inside audit-tools, and the result still trails ecosystem-native build knowledge. Retire these in-tree semantic analyzers in favor of acquired producers of a standard symbol/index representation such as SCIP, LSIF, or a small normalized symbol-relation stream emitted by ecosystem-native compiler or language-server adapters. Keep only the language-agnostic manifest/regex floor and one importer in core; resolve and cache index producers through the existing acquisition mechanism. This turns language coverage into data-driven adapter acquisition, improves resolution fidelity, and removes the perpetual per-language implementation ladder without changing downstream graph consumers.

findings.title: Compile both products from declarative workflow-node descriptors
findings.summary: The shared obligation engine centralizes only the priority scan and transition/emit fold; its contract deliberately leaves satisfaction derivation, executor mapping, host gates, and persistence to each product. These controllers manually assemble preambles, incoming-file handshakes, pause/resume behavior, no-progress and cycle guards, step rendering, transition bookkeeping, and terminal routing. Replace them with one workflow runtime driven by typed node descriptors declaring dependencies, satisfaction projection, executor, accepted input schema, produced artifacts/write set, host barrier, resource class, retry policy, and convergence rule. Audit and remediation should provide only domain state projections and domain actions; the runtime should derive ready work, validate responses, persist transitions, and render step contracts. This makes a new phase or host gate a descriptor addition instead of another branch in a product-specific mega-controller, while preserving genuinely different audit and remediation policy.

findings.title: Conceptual-review panels lack an ownership and generation boundary
findings.summary: The per-process step slots isolate prompts, but the deep conceptual-review panel itself still uses shared, fixed incoming filenames and a family-wide lease namespace. prepareConceptualDispatch can therefore create the same perspective and judge targets for concurrent or retried panels, while handleDesignReviewBranch releases the design-review leases when either incoming pass is observed. A late worker or a second invocation can overwrite or mix generations, release another panel's leases, and let the judge merge a hybrid set that has no single owner. This is corroborated by the adversarial review and is higher impact than ordinary file-collision risk because the panel's output controls whether the design-review obligation is considered complete. findings.title: Make audit execution commit typed artifact deltas instead of replacing the full bundle
findings.summary: A normal executor identifies one or two changed artifacts in artifacts_written, yet the persistence path still carries a complete updated_bundle: computeArtifactMetadata hashes every present DAG artifact, writeCoreArtifacts serially rewrites every registered artifact under the bundle lock, and loadArtifactBundle serially reparses the whole set. executeAdvance also rebuilds its line index by rereading every manifest file before it knows whether the selected operation needs line counts. In this run that means repeatedly processing roughly 14.9 MB of top-level artifacts and 727 source files for transitions that often change one small JSON document; the full-bundle replacement contract also forces the global bundle-mutation mutex described by the concurrency design. Replace ExecutorRunResult.updated with a mechanically enforced ArtifactDelta carrying typed set/delete operations, derive metadata and tombstones from that delta, commit each key with dependency-revision compare-and-swap, and load only the selected obligation's dependency closure. Materialize content-bound line counts during intake and reuse them until file-integrity invalidation. This makes omitted write declarations impossible by construction, preserves prune/staleness semantics, removes most parse/hash/write work, shortens lock holds, and permits independent DAG branches to commit concurrently.

findings.summary: The audit treats repository drift as work to chase: deterministic stages inspect the live checkout, while in-process semantic dispatch creates a detached HEAD snapshot per drive, removes it, and deliberately recreates it so a later drive sees a newer commit. findings.title: Run acquired analyzers in disposable least-privilege capsules
findings.summary: Analyzer safety is currently expressed as pinned versions, consent, capability probes, and argv builders that promise read-only flags, but admitted npx, pipx, cargo, bundle, and downloaded binaries still execute directly in the audited repository with the host process environment and filesystem authority; report-producing tools even create and remove files under that root. Replace convention-based read-only execution with one analyzer capsule abstraction: an immutable source snapshot mounted or copied read-only, a dedicated writable scratch/output directory, scrubbed credentials and environment, explicit network policy, resource/time limits, and a typed output channel. Use native sandbox/container facilities when available and a disposable snapshot runner as the portable fallback, recording the achieved isolation level in analyzer status. This makes acquisition reproducible, prevents analyzer caches and reports from contaminating the source generation, and mechanically contains third-party tooling rather than trusting every candidate's flags and behavior.

findings.title: Session configuration mixes intent, capability, and effective execution
findings.summary: SessionConfig remains the aggregate consumed by persistence, validation, provider construction, quota assembly, and orchestration even though the design now distinguishes repository intent from per-auditor capability. RepoSessionIntent is derived through omission lists, while resolveSessionConfig overlays descriptor and ambient fields onto another SessionConfig; capability-like fields such as quota, block-quota, and host dispatch status still sit beside persisted policy. A new field therefore requires synchronized negative lists, known-key sets, validators, and precedence logic, and partially resolved states can survive until a later consumer. The elegance review identified this boundary leak. Define explicit persisted RepoIntent, per-auditor Capabilities, and EffectiveExecutionConfig types with one conversion step, and make runtime consumers accept only the effective form.

findings.title: Stale steal-claim reclamation can delete a fresh claim
findings.summary: The main lock is protected by token-checked deletion, but the .steal sidecar is reclaimed using stat followed by an unconditional unlink. findings.title: Treat lenses as coverage obligations instead of task identities
findings.summary: Planning expands repository topology into a file-by-lens work matrix and then spends another subsystem recombining those rows: unitBuilder assigns commonly two to five required lenses, taskBuilder groups pending paths separately for each lens, the affinity graph reconnects cross-lens tasks that cite the same files, and packetPrompt requires one repetitive AuditResult wrapper per task even though it tells the worker to review the packet once. findings.title: Use one segmented content-addressed graph store through enrichment and decomposition
findings.summary: Incrementality stops at the regex-floor edge cache: the current run persists a 2.47 MB graph-edge-cache beside a 3.26 MB expanded graph_bundle containing much of the same edge payload, while enrichment reconstructs whole merged edge arrays and the TypeScript analyzer creates a fresh non-incremental Program on every pass. Nine graph-enrichment runs consumed 69,086 ms and seven decomposition runs another 63,294 ms. Make content-addressed per-file/per-analyzer graph segments authoritative, keyed by file content, analyzer identity/version/config, and path-world revision; let graph_bundle be a compact manifest over those segments, invalidate only affected dependency neighborhoods, and warm-start decomposition from unchanged communities. Consumers can materialize only the relation slices they need. This removes duplicate graph storage and carries incremental reuse across semantic enrichment and decomposition rather than discarding it at the floor boundary.

findings.title: Cross-process coordination is a database-shaped protocol built from JSON files
findings.summary: Claims, quota reservations, lock stealing, heartbeats, expiry, and read-modify-write state updates form a cross-process coordination substrate, but they are spread across bespoke sidecar locks and JSON stores. ClaimRegistry explicitly degrades malformed state to an empty map, which can re-grant a live node; similar recovery and lease semantics are implemented again in the reservation and locked-store layers. This is corroborated by the novelty review and is a correctness boundary, not merely a storage preference. Consolidate claims, reservations, and mutable run state behind one transactionally defined persistence adapter with schema/version migration, uniqueness, token-checked lease expiry, and crash recovery; keep JSON for export/report artifacts. If a native embedded database is not portable for the supported runtime, use one maintained lock-plus-atomic-write implementation behind that adapter rather than extending parallel protocols.

findings.summary: Repository policy is implemented as 18 separate check:* commands plus hook and release gates, while the representative custom check/generator programs alone total about 2,766 lines. findings.title: Run independent external analyzers through a bounded parallel scheduler
findings.summary: External analyzer acquisition is a two-stage serial pipeline: resolveBinaryCandidates awaits every detected binary resolution one at a time, then runAcquisitionEngine executes every registered analyzer synchronously in registry order. This preserves deterministic artifacts and the single spawn-admission gate while reducing acquisition wall time toward the slowest admitted analyzer rather than the sum of them.

findings.title: Use sparse community incidence for multi-resolution decomposition
findings.summary: The decomposition pipeline runs five independent Louvain passes for each behavior graph, then coMembershipCounts expands every community in every partition into all unordered member pairs. The later scoring stage explicitly treats communities larger than max(50, 20% of the universe) as non-evidence, but those coarse communities have already paid quadratic pair-generation and map costs during candidate formation. The current 1,369-node run repeatedly spends about 8-11 seconds in structure_decomposition_executor to produce three consensus and six contested subsystems. Represent each partition as sparse community-to-member incidence, exclude or down-weight oversized communities before candidate generation, reuse one normalized adjacency across the resolution ladder, and evaluate candidate intersections directly; independent source ladders can run in bounded parallel workers. This preserves deterministic, language-neutral agreement scoring while making work proportional to informative memberships rather than dense coarse clusters.

findings.title: Replace serial systemic-challenge rounds with parallel adversary waves
findings.summary: The challenge loop dispatches exactly one generalist adversary, ingests one systemic-challenge.json, then requires another next-step boundary before the next round; this prompt is round 8. Novelty search is naturally parallel: issue a bounded wave of adversaries with disjoint pressure assignments such as control-plane simplification, cross-run reuse, concurrency, and whole-subsystem replacement, then deterministically ground and cross-dedupe their submissions together. A wave is dry only when every branch adds nothing after the shared fold; any new finding seeds the next wave. Reuse the existing atomic host-fanout quota gate for admission. This retains the strict loop-until-dry criterion while reducing serial LLM latency and avoiding the narrowing effect of one agent repeatedly conditioning on its own prior search path.

themes.title: Conceptual Design & Architecture Abstraction Boundaries
themes.root_cause: Lifecycle management, semantic analysis, and provider integration suffer from conceptual design coupling, relying on monolithic controllers, unconstrained optional-field schemas, and shape-based review checks instead of explicit capability driver protocols and deterministic state machine descriptors.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Replace monolithic controllers with typed workflow node descriptors, decouple provider integrations into out-of-core capability drivers, acquire standard semantic indexes (e.g. SCIP/LSIF), and enforce immutable generation manifests for conceptual review panels.

themes.title: Observational Contract Enforcement & Orchestration Race Conditions
themes.root_cause: State transition functions and dispatch loops fail to strictly enforce observational behavioral contracts, allowing un-mutexed claim overwrites, unhandled DAG self-loops, stale state reuse, and cross-process admission races.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Enforce strict atomic state transitions under mutex locks, pass pre-merge edit snapshots directly to overlap detectors, reject self-referential DAG nodes, and validate all input payload shapes and reader paths.

themes.title: Data Integrity, Schema Validation & State Deserialization Deficiencies
themes.root_cause: State loaders, token parsers, and input ingestion functions swallow parsing errors or perform loose type casting, falling back to empty structures and allowing corrupted or partial data to overwrite persistent snapshots.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Implement comprehensive schema validation (e.g. Zod schemas) for all persisted state and input payloads, eliminate permissive empty-object fallbacks on JSON parse failures, and route all file mutations through read-only snapshot remediation pipelines.

themes.title: Reliability, Non-Idempotent External Actions & Crash Recovery
themes.root_cause: External side-effects (git push, PR creation, release publishing) execute before persisting phase completion or pre-execution journals, causing duplicate operations on retry and stranding partial workflow states.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Write durable pre-execution journals prior to running external side effects, pin audit stages to single content-addressed source generations, add explicit deadlines to HTTP probes, and preserve command output across workflow failures.

themes.title: Security Isolation & Permission Boundary Deficiencies
themes.root_cause: Security checks fail open when dispatch plans are missing, permission bypass flags are evaluated without strict boolean parsing, untrusted plan inputs are passed directly to shell execution, and acquired tooling runs with host privileges.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Execute untrusted plan commands and acquired analyzers in disposable least-privilege containers/capsules with scrubbed environments, fail closed when ownership plans are unreadable, and enforce strict type checking on security configuration flags.

themes.title: Test Suite Verification Deficits & Performance Overhead
themes.root_cause: The test suite contains vacuous assertions, relies on local reimplementations of production logic, pins erroneous behavior, omits negative and concurrency edge cases, and suffers from heavy OS/Git process setup overhead.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Refactor unit and integration tests to invoke canonical production logic directly, remove tautological/vacuous assertions, add negative test coverage for corrupted state and concurrency races, and adopt an in-memory deterministic scenario runtime.

executive_summary: The audit of audit-tools revealed critical vulnerabilities across core execution orchestrators, state persistence, security boundaries, and testing suites. Systemic risks stem from weak schema validation of state and input artifacts, non-idempotent external publication side effects, unisolated execution of analyzer tools and plan commands, and conceptual design coupling between lifecycle management and product-specific drivers. Resolving these issues requires adopting explicit capability driver abstractions, fail-closed validation on all state transitions, and deterministic scenario testing.
top_risks: Conceptual Design Risk: Monolithic lifecycle controllers and unconstrained abstractions force complex manual artifact intervention during non-convergence and prevent clean separation of provider and analyzer capabilities.

Observational Contract Risk: Closing phase side effects (git push, PR creation, release publishing) run before durable state updates, leading to duplicate external actions on process crashes or resumes.
Security & Isolation Risk: Untrusted plan commands reach host shells and missing dispatch plans disable rolling write-scope boundaries, exposing host resources and allowing unowned file mutations.

Data Integrity Risk: Malformed or unreadable JSON files (owner tokens, pending tasks, dispatch plans) default to permissive or empty states rather than failing closed, corrupting claims and state transitions.

Verification Risk: Test suite gaps—including vacuous assertions, tests pinning invalid behavior, and missing negative tests for unreadable states—mask critical regressions across orchestration and merge logic.
